bib.title: A Scalable Hierarchical Distributed Language Model
bib.venue: NeurIPS 2008 (Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 21)

question: Can a hierarchical (binary-tree softmax) neural language model with automatically built word trees match or beat non-hierarchical neural and n-gram models while training orders of magnitude faster?
hypothesis: A carefully constructed, data-driven word hierarchy (with words allowed multiple codes) lets a hierarchical log-bilinear model outperform the non-hierarchical LBL and n-gram models.
contributions: Hierarchical log-bilinear model (HLBL) using diagonal context matrices and a single predicted vector per prediction
Simple feature-based algorithm (bootstrapped, recursive 2-Gaussian mixture) to build word trees from data
Support for multiple codes per word (overcomplete trees)

method.summary: HLBL replaces the LBL softmax with a product of binary logistic decisions along a path in a word tree, each node having its own feature vector. Trees are built by training an HLBL on a random tree, averaging each word's predicted feature vectors over its contexts, then recursively clustering with 2-component Gaussian mixtures (EM, 10 steps).

datasets.name: APNews
datasets.source: Associated Press news stories 1995-1996, used earlier in Bengio et al. 2003 and Mnih & Hinton 2007

models.name: HLBL
models.architecture: hierarchical log-bilinear; diagonal context weight matrices, node feature vectors, logistic node decisions

other.source: scores from Mnih & Hinton 2007, timing from authors' implementation

training.lr: 1e-3, then 3e-5 after validation perplexity first rises
training.lr_schedule: two-stage: train at 10^-3 until validation perplexity increases, drop to 3x10^-5 and resume until it increases again
training.regularisation: small L2 penalty on all parameters (value not stated); early stopping on validation perplexity
training.wall_clock: 4 to 32 min per epoch for HLBL; 6420 min per epoch for LBL

other.init: Gaussian of small variance (not specified); tree-node biases set to match word base rates
other.tree_building: EM 10 steps, spherical covariances, tree built in a few minutes for ~18000 words with 100-dim vectors

inference.samples: not stated; tree construction is randomised, one tree per algorithm generated

parameters.overcomplete: 2x and 4x trees via root joining multiple ADAPTIVE(0.4) trees

eval.protocol: single runs; no seeds, variances or significance tests reported

results.claim: A 2x overcomplete ADAPTIVE(0.4) HLBL beats the non-hierarchical LBL (117.0) and both KN n-grams.
results.setup: APNews (14M word train, 1M val, 1M test, vocab 17964), 100-dim features, context 5
results.table: Table 3, row HLBL T6 ADAPTIVE(0.4) x 2, column Perplexity

results.claim: A 4x overcomplete tree gives the best perplexity, 112.1, at 32 min/epoch.
results.setup: APNews (14M word train, 1M val, 1M test, vocab 17964), 100-dim features, context 5
results.table: Table 3, row HLBL T7 ADAPTIVE(0.4) x 4, column Perplexity

results.claim: The slowest HLBL is over 200 times faster per epoch than LBL (6420 vs 32 min).
results.setup: APNews (14M word train, 1M val, 1M test, vocab 17964), 100-dim features, context 5
results.quote: Indeed, the slowest of our HLBL models is over 200 times faster than the LBL model.

results.claim: Random-tree HLBL gets 151.2 perplexity vs 131.3 for the BALANCED data-driven tree, same speed (4 min/epoch).
results.setup: APNews (14M word train, 1M val, 1M test, vocab 17964), 100-dim features, context 5
results.table: Table 3, row HLBL T2 BALANCED, column Perplexity

results.claim: ADAPTIVE (unbalanced) tree improves over BALANCED at same cost.
results.setup: APNews (14M word train, 1M val, 1M test, vocab 17964), 100-dim features, context 5
results.table: Table 3, row HLBL T3 ADAPTIVE, column Perplexity

results.claim: KN5 and KN3 n-gram perplexities (from Mnih & Hinton 2007).
results.setup: APNews (14M word train, 1M val, 1M test, vocab 17964), 100-dim features, context 5

results.claim: Non-random tree reduces perplexity by 19.9 at 100 dims (151.2 to 131.3), and by 29.2 at 25 dims.
results.setup: APNews (14M word train, 1M val, 1M test, vocab 17964), 100-dim features, context 5 (dims varied 25-100)
results.table: Table 2, row 100, column Reduction in perplexity

results.claim: Unigram model perplexity; random-tree HLBL beats it by a large margin.
results.setup: APNews (14M word train, 1M val, 1M test, vocab 17964), 100-dim features, context 5
results.quote: they outperform the unigram model which achieved the perplexity of 602.0 by a very large margin

results.claim: Mean code length grows with overcompleteness (14.2 random to 143.2 for 4x), raising cost and parameters.
results.setup: APNews (14M word train, 1M val, 1M test, vocab 17964), 100-dim features, context 5
results.table: Table 1, row T7 ADAPTIVE(0.4) x 4, column Mean code length

results.claim: Tree-building took only a few minutes for a vocabulary of nearly 18000 words with 100-dim vectors.
Words with most codes were infrequent, hard-to-cluster words, not multi-sense words.

limits: One dataset (APNews, 14M words), single runs, no variance or significance tests
Batch size, L2 strength, init variance, hardware, epochs and code not stated
Multiple codes replicate rare words, not multi-sense words (authors concede)
Overcomplete trees add parameters and cost linearly (32 min/epoch for 4x); comparison to LBL uses LBL/KN scores from an earlier paper
Authors propose but do not test periodic tree rebuilding during training

terms.definition: binary string of decisions that specifies the path from root to a word's leaf
tree in which each word occurs more than once, built by joining multiple generated trees under one root
